1	# PRD – Regional Storefronts, Consent & Routing
2	
3	*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Regional Storefronts", "Country to Storefront Mapping", and "Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL". Last updated: 2026-06-19. SFCC site IDs and locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 BM (2026-06-13).*
4	
5	---
6	
7	## 1. Storefronts & URL Prefixes (REG-001 – REG-008, REG-043, DMU-013, DMU-016)
8	
9	**7 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions in Business Manager:** AU, US, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME. A MX domestic site is planned for 2027. EU domestic and EU international remain **separate sites** (REG-006).
10	
11	> **Status (2026-06-11):** REG-005 is **Confirmed** — the US storefront is a **single SFCC site** supporting BOTH a domestic checkout path (SFCC-owned) AND an international checkout path (Global-e-owned) within the same site; the path is determined by the customer's shipping address. The `/us/` and `/en-ca/` URL prefixes both map to the one US site. Rationale (IC comment 25.05, now confirmed): shared US inventory pool, unified reporting (domestic + international rolled up), shared content/navigation; prices per market. Note: REG-001 carries an earlier 05.05 IC comment recommending sites be kept separate to manage Global-e complexity — this was superseded by the confirmed REG-005 single-site decision.
12	
13	Each storefront has its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods, configured independently (REG-002).
14	
15	11 active locales across the 7 sites (REG-043). EU domestic and EU international are separate storefronts (REG-006).
16	
17	SFCC site IDs and BM locale IDs (verified 2026-06-13):
18	
19	| Locale | SFCC Site ID | BM Locale ID | URL prefix | Local currency | Checkout owner |
20	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
21	| AU (+ Oceania) | `ZimmermannAU` | `en` | `/` (root; x-default hreflang) | AUD | SFCC (REG-003) |
22	| UK | `ZimmermannUK` | `en-GB` | `/uk/` | GBP | SFCC (REG-004) |
23	| US (domestic path) | `ZimmermannUS` | `en-US` | `/us/` | USD | SFCC (REG-005) |
24	| US (international path, same site) | `ZimmermannUS` | `en-US` | `/en-ca/` | USD | Global-e (REG-005, branched by shipping address — no separate locale) |
25	| EU domestic (EN) | `ZimmermannEU` | `en-GB` | `/en-eu/` | EUR | SFCC (REG-006 dom) |
26	| EU domestic (FR) | `ZimmermannEU` | `fr` | `/fr-eu/` | EUR | SFCC |
27	| EU domestic (IT) | `ZimmermannEU` | `it` | `/it-eu/` | EUR | SFCC |
28	| EU domestic (ES) | `ZimmermannEU` | `es` | `/es-eu/` | EUR | SFCC |
29	| EU international | `ZimmermannEUIntl` | `en-CH` | `/en-ch/` | EUR | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
30	| HK | `ZimmermannHK` | `en-HK` | `/hk/` | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-007) |
31	| ME | `ZimmermannME` | `en-AE` | `/en-ae/` | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-008) |
32	
33	ROW also routed via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` prefixes (DMU-013; see [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md) for full URL strategy). AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — the AU root remains globally crawlable because search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the human geo-redirect; see REG-009 in Section 4).
34	
35	URL formats: product `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` (the `.html` suffix is **preserved** to maintain existing indexed URLs — DMU-015); category `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no `.html`). Category URLs are updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`) with 301 redirects from all legacy paths (DMU-014).
36	
37	Business users can manage storefront configuration in SFCC BM at both global and individual storefront levels (REG-010).
38	
39	The US storefront supports all required US address formats; APO, FPO, and PO Box addresses are **not** supported (REG-012).
40	
41	### Country → Storefront routing (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet)
42	
43	The full per-country mapping lives in the source sheet; the FE only needs the routing logic:
44	
45	- **AU (root):** Australia (default) and all Oceania — American Samoa, Cook Islands, Fiji, Guam, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Northern Marianas, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu. NZ and New Caledonia get Avalara duty/tax; other Oceania destinations are DDU (REG-003).
46	- **UK (`/uk/`):** United Kingdom only.
47	- **US (`/us/` domestic):** United States (default) and **Puerto Rico**.
48	- **US (`/en-ca/` international, Global-e):** Canada, Mexico, and all other Americas — Caribbean, Central America, and South America (Argentina, Aruba, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, Bolivia, Brazil, BVI, Cayman, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Grenada, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad & Tobago, Turks & Caicos, USVI, Uruguay, Venezuela, etc.).
49	- **EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`):** France (default), Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Ireland, Portugal, Greece, **Denmark**, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino.
50	- **EU international (`/en-ch/`, Global-e):** Non-EU Europe (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Gibraltar, Greenland, Faroe Islands, Channel Islands, etc.) and **all of Africa** (Algeria, Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cape Verde, Chad, Comoros, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Réunion, São Tomé, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Also includes Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname.
51	- **HK (`/hk/`, Global-e):** Hong Kong (default), China, Macau, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Maldives, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Timor-Leste, Uzbekistan. **Also includes "Australia" as a destination** — this is the REG-027 path for non-Oceania clients who select AU in the country selector (they are routed to HK, not the gated AU site).
52	- **ME (`/en-ae/`, Global-e):** UAE (default), Bahrain, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia.
53	
54	**Denmark routing is resolved → EU Domestic** (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet confirms; remove from Open Items).
55	
56	> Geographic anomalies (mapping sheet): Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname all route to **EU International** despite being in the Americas/African geography. This follows fulfilment territory, not landmass — flagged for awareness; routing tables must follow the sheet verbatim.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## 2. Entry Routing & Mismatch Detection (REG-009, REG-013 – REG-035)
61	
62	- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
63	- **AU is gated** to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IPs only (REG-009). AU is the `x-default` hreflang and must remain crawlable, so it is never blocked at the network level. A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. Image/News, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, AppleBot, YandexBot, Baiduspider, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, Discordbot). Fail open: if UA looks botty but isn't matched, skip the redirect rather than apply it — false-positive cost is zero, missing a real crawler hurts SEO.
64	- All other storefronts use **mismatch detection** (REG-014): a country slide-out is shown on the first visit if the user's IP country does not match the storefront's shipping region (REG-015). Two CTAs: redirect to the appropriate storefront, or open the country selector (REG-016). A warning is shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-017). Not shown if country matches (REG-018). Shown on first visit only — does not reappear after selection or dismissal (REG-019).
65	- **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU (REG-020, REG-025). Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field (REG-021). Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, all other storefronts English only (REG-023). Selected EU locale reflected in URL (REG-024).
66	- AU is gated and does **not** allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites (REG-025).
67	- **China** selected from any country selector routes to HK (REG-026).
68	- **Australia** selected from another storefront's country selector (i.e. clients outside Oceania) routes to HK (REG-027).
69	- Global-e checkout locks the shipping country — determined by country selector pre-checkout, cannot be changed inside Global-e (REG-028).
70	
71	### EU language mismatch (REG-029 – REG-035)
72	When a user's GEO-IP country doesn't match the URL language on the EU domestic storefront, show a language mismatch modal in the current URL language (REG-029, REG-031). Two CTAs: continue in current language, or switch (REG-032). Country-to-language mapping (REG-030):
73	- France / Monaco → French (`/fr-eu/`)
74	- Italy / San Marino → Italian (`/it-eu/`)
75	- Spain → Spanish (`/es-eu/`)
76	
77	Modal does not show when detected country matches the current URL language (REG-033), and is not shown for countries with no dedicated EU locale — they default to `/en-eu/` (REG-034). Logic applies regardless of entry point (Instagram, Google Shopping, direct URL, organic search) (REG-035).
78	
79	---
80	
81	## 3. Checkout Ownership
82	
83	- **SFCC** owns domestic checkout for AU (REG-003), UK (REG-004), US domestic (REG-005), EU domestic (REG-006 dom).
84	- **Global-e** owns checkout for HK (REG-007), ME (REG-008), US international (REG-005, path determined by shipping address within the US site), EU international (REG-006 intl) — and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market.
85	- **AU serves Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands) domestically** via SFCC — not via Global-e. Avalara calculates duties/tax for NZ and New Caledonia specifically (REG-003); other Oceania destinations are DDU.
86	- Branch checkout ownership at PDP/cart, not only at the checkout page.
87	- **Global-e pricing via SFCC price books (REG-041, Confirmed 05-05):** SFCC holds all price books including for Global-e markets. AP21 feeds base RRP pricebooks per currency (AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) and fixed pricelists per Global-e market to SFCC via MuleSoft. A nightly job generates Global-e-derived pricebooks using FX rates and coefficients from Global-e. Global-e handles shipping charges, duties, and taxes at checkout. SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency to Global-e. SFCC does **not** independently calculate shipping, duties, or tax for Global-e paths. (REG-040 was retired 05-05 — superseded by REG-041.)
88	
89	*For checkout-specific frontend behaviour (redirect trigger, data flow), see [checkout.md](checkout.md).*

91	---

94	
95	- Single currency per domestic storefront: AUD, USD, GBP, EUR (REG-039). No multi-currency toggle. (Open: Zimmermann would like multi-currency on AU domestic to offer NZD — not yet agreed.)
96	- Tax display: AU (GST), UK (VAT) via SFCC native tax tables, EU domestic (VAT) via Avalara (REG-037). The EU domestic site supports one RRP but must support multiple EU zone VAT requirements in the order payload. US domestic: prices excl. tax; Avalara calculates sales tax at checkout (REG-038). NZ and New Caledonia on AU: Avalara (REG-037).
97	- Sale pricing: was/now format. If price changes again after sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042).
98	- Prices shown in storefront currency on PDP, PLP, mini-cart, cart (REG-036).

102	## 5. EU Locale Billing Fields (REG-011)
103	
104	The system will display locale-specific additional billing fields where required (e.g. Italian Codice Fiscale or VAT ID). **Open (REG-011):** confirm with Egaltine which other locales (e.g. Spanish NIF, French SIRET) require additional fields. Do not implement until confirmed.

106	---

108	## 6. Language & Translation (REG-044 – REG-047)
109	
110	- EU domestic supports 4 languages: EN, FR, IT, ES (REG-044). All other storefronts English only.
111	- All customer-facing content (CMS from Contentful, product data from Product API) translated across EU locale variants (REG-045). CMS must accommodate translation-driven adjustments (e.g. button resize for translated CTAs).

Translation occurs directly between **Contentful and Transperfect** outside the PWA Kit's concern; any SFCC-held strings (e.g. system messages, validation copy) are translated via static JSON files. No FE work required beyond consuming the translated Contentful payloads.

117	## 7. Consent (Didomi) (REG-048 – REG-056)

119	- Cookie consent banner shown on first visit on all storefronts, managed by Didomi CMP (REG-048). Consent preferences persist across sessions (REG-050).

133	- Hashed email passed to GTM at order confirmation for Enhanced Conversions (REG-056).
134	- Didomi consent notice greys out all site content and prevents interaction until the consent flow completes (HPC-013/014).

139

141	- Opt-in state sync: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys. Passed to Omneo on order placement for guests, on account registration for registered customers (REG-058).

# PRD – Regional Storefronts, Consent & Routing

*Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx, sheets "Regional Storefronts", "Country to Storefront Mapping", and "Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL". Last updated: 2026-06-19. SFCC site IDs and locale IDs verified against bkzk-002 BM (2026-06-13).*

---

## 1. Storefronts & URL Prefixes (REG-001 – REG-008, REG-043, DMU-013, DMU-016)

**7 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions in Business Manager:** AU, US, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME. A MX domestic site is planned for 2027. EU domestic and EU international remain **separate sites** (REG-006).

> **Status (2026-06-11):** REG-005 is **Confirmed** — the US storefront is a **single SFCC site** supporting BOTH a domestic checkout path (SFCC-owned) AND an international checkout path (Global-e-owned) within the same site; the path is determined by the customer's shipping address. The `/us/` and `/en-ca/` URL prefixes both map to the one US site. Rationale (IC comment 25.05, now confirmed): shared US inventory pool, unified reporting (domestic + international rolled up), shared content/navigation; prices per market. Note: REG-001 carries an earlier 05.05 IC comment recommending sites be kept separate to manage Global-e complexity — this was superseded by the confirmed REG-005 single-site decision.

Each storefront has its own currency, tax model, locale set, delivery options, and payment methods, configured independently (REG-002).

11 active locales across the 7 sites (REG-043). EU domestic and EU international are separate storefronts (REG-006).

SFCC site IDs and BM locale IDs (verified 2026-06-13):

| Locale | SFCC Site ID | BM Locale ID | URL prefix | Local currency | Checkout owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AU (+ Oceania) | `ZimmermannAU` | `en` | `/` (root; x-default hreflang) | AUD | SFCC (REG-003) |
| UK | `ZimmermannUK` | `en-GB` | `/uk/` | GBP | SFCC (REG-004) |
| US (domestic path) | `ZimmermannUS` | `en-US` | `/us/` | USD | SFCC (REG-005) |
| US (international path, same site) | `ZimmermannUS` | `en-US` | `/en-ca/` | USD | Global-e (REG-005, branched by shipping address — no separate locale) |
| EU domestic (EN) | `ZimmermannEU` | `en-GB` | `/en-eu/` | EUR | SFCC (REG-006 dom) |
| EU domestic (FR) | `ZimmermannEU` | `fr` | `/fr-eu/` | EUR | SFCC |
| EU domestic (IT) | `ZimmermannEU` | `it` | `/it-eu/` | EUR | SFCC |
| EU domestic (ES) | `ZimmermannEU` | `es` | `/es-eu/` | EUR | SFCC |
| EU international | `ZimmermannEUIntl` | `en-CH` | `/en-ch/` | EUR | Global-e (REG-006 intl) |
| HK | `ZimmermannHK` | `en-HK` | `/hk/` | HKD (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-007) |
| ME | `ZimmermannME` | `en-AE` | `/en-ae/` | AED (SFCC price books) | Global-e (REG-008) |

ROW also routed via `/en-ch/` and `/en-ca/` prefixes (DMU-013; see [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md) for full URL strategy). AU configured as root with no locale prefix and designated x-default hreflang target (DMU-016, **Resolved** — the AU root remains globally crawlable because search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the human geo-redirect; see REG-009 in Section 4).

URL formats: product `/[prefix]/[name]-[colour].html` (the `.html` suffix is **preserved** to maintain existing indexed URLs — DMU-015); category `/[prefix]/[slug]` (no `.html`). Category URLs are updated for SEO consolidation (e.g. `/clothing/dresses`) with 301 redirects from all legacy paths (DMU-014).

Business users can manage storefront configuration in SFCC BM at both global and individual storefront levels (REG-010).

The US storefront supports all required US address formats; APO, FPO, and PO Box addresses are **not** supported (REG-012).

### Country → Storefront routing (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet)

The full per-country mapping lives in the source sheet; the FE only needs the routing logic:

- **AU (root):** Australia (default) and all Oceania — American Samoa, Cook Islands, Fiji, Guam, Kiribati, Marshall Islands, Micronesia, Nauru, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Niue, Northern Marianas, Palau, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu. NZ and New Caledonia get Avalara duty/tax; other Oceania destinations are DDU (REG-003).
- **UK (`/uk/`):** United Kingdom only.
- **US (`/us/` domestic):** United States (default) and **Puerto Rico**.
- **US (`/en-ca/` international, Global-e):** Canada, Mexico, and all other Americas — Caribbean, Central America, and South America (Argentina, Aruba, Bahamas, Barbados, Belize, Bermuda, Bolivia, Brazil, BVI, Cayman, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Grenada, Guatemala, Guyana, Haiti, Honduras, Jamaica, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, St Kitts & Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent, Trinidad & Tobago, Turks & Caicos, USVI, Uruguay, Venezuela, etc.).
- **EU domestic (`/en-eu/`, `/fr-eu/`, `/it-eu/`, `/es-eu/`):** France (default), Germany, Italy, Spain, Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Austria, Ireland, Portugal, Greece, **Denmark**, Sweden, Finland, Poland, Czechia, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, Croatia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Cyprus, Malta, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Andorra, Monaco, San Marino.
- **EU international (`/en-ch/`, Global-e):** Non-EU Europe (Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Albania, Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Gibraltar, Greenland, Faroe Islands, Channel Islands, etc.) and **all of Africa** (Algeria, Angola, Benin, Botswana, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Cape Verde, Chad, Comoros, Congo, Côte d'Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Lesotho, Liberia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Mozambique, Namibia, Nigeria, Réunion, São Tomé, Senegal, Seychelles, Sierra Leone, South Africa, Swaziland, Tanzania, Togo, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe). Also includes Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname.
- **HK (`/hk/`, Global-e):** Hong Kong (default), China, Macau, Taiwan, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Philippines, India, Bangladesh, Bhutan, Brunei, Cambodia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Laos, Maldives, Mongolia, Myanmar, Nepal, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Tajikistan, Timor-Leste, Uzbekistan. **Also includes "Australia" as a destination** — this is the REG-027 path for non-Oceania clients who select AU in the country selector (they are routed to HK, not the gated AU site).
- **ME (`/en-ae/`, Global-e):** UAE (default), Bahrain, Egypt, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia.

**Denmark routing is resolved → EU Domestic** (Country to Storefront Mapping sheet confirms; remove from Open Items).

> Geographic anomalies (mapping sheet): Falkland Islands, French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique, Mayotte, Saint Barthélemy, Saint Helena, Saint Martin, Suriname all route to **EU International** despite being in the Americas/African geography. This follows fulfilment territory, not landmass — flagged for awareness; routing tables must follow the sheet verbatim.

---

## 2. Entry Routing & Mismatch Detection (REG-009, REG-013 – REG-035)

- **IP geolocation** selects the site on first visit (REG-013).
- **AU is gated** to AU and NZ/Pacific Island IPs only (REG-009). AU is the `x-default` hreflang and must remain crawlable, so it is never blocked at the network level. A non-AU/non-Oceania human visitor landing on AU is redirected server-side to their matched storefront before AUD pricing renders; if no storefront matches their region, fall back to HK. Search-engine and social-unfurler bots are exempt from the redirect — match by User-Agent against a comprehensive allowlist (Googlebot incl. Image/News, Bingbot, DuckDuckBot, AppleBot, YandexBot, Baiduspider, Slackbot, Twitterbot, facebookexternalhit, LinkedInBot, WhatsApp, Discordbot). Fail open: if UA looks botty but isn't matched, skip the redirect rather than apply it — false-positive cost is zero, missing a real crawler hurts SEO.
- All other storefronts use **mismatch detection** (REG-014): a country slide-out is shown on the first visit if the user's IP country does not match the storefront's shipping region (REG-015). Two CTAs: redirect to the appropriate storefront, or open the country selector (REG-016). A warning is shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-017). Not shown if country matches (REG-018). Shown on first visit only — does not reappear after selection or dismissal (REG-019).
- **Country + language selector** available on all storefronts except AU (REG-020, REG-025). Countries grouped by region (Asia/Oceania, Europe, Americas) with currency display and search field (REG-021). Warning shown that changing location may remove items from the bag (REG-022). Country and language combined in the same selector; EU domestic offers EN/FR/IT/ES, all other storefronts English only (REG-023). Selected EU locale reflected in URL (REG-024).
- AU is gated and does **not** allow inbound cross-navigation from other sites (REG-025).
- **China** selected from any country selector routes to HK (REG-026).
- **Australia** selected from another storefront's country selector (i.e. clients outside Oceania) routes to HK (REG-027).
- Global-e checkout locks the shipping country — determined by country selector pre-checkout, cannot be changed inside Global-e (REG-028).

### EU language mismatch (REG-029 – REG-035)
When a user's GEO-IP country doesn't match the URL language on the EU domestic storefront, show a language mismatch modal in the current URL language (REG-029, REG-031). Two CTAs: continue in current language, or switch (REG-032). Country-to-language mapping (REG-030):
- France / Monaco → French (`/fr-eu/`)
- Italy / San Marino → Italian (`/it-eu/`)
- Spain → Spanish (`/es-eu/`)

Modal does not show when detected country matches the current URL language (REG-033), and is not shown for countries with no dedicated EU locale — they default to `/en-eu/` (REG-034). Logic applies regardless of entry point (Instagram, Google Shopping, direct URL, organic search) (REG-035).

---

## 3. Checkout Ownership

- **SFCC** owns domestic checkout for AU (REG-003), UK (REG-004), US domestic (REG-005), EU domestic (REG-006 dom).
- **Global-e** owns checkout for HK (REG-007), ME (REG-008), US international (REG-005, path determined by shipping address within the US site), EU international (REG-006 intl) — and for any domestic storefront when the customer's selected shipping destination is outside the domestic market.
- **AU serves Oceania (NZ, New Caledonia, Pacific Islands) domestically** via SFCC — not via Global-e. Avalara calculates duties/tax for NZ and New Caledonia specifically (REG-003); other Oceania destinations are DDU.
- Branch checkout ownership at PDP/cart, not only at the checkout page.
- **Global-e pricing via SFCC price books (REG-041, Confirmed 05-05):** SFCC holds all price books including for Global-e markets. AP21 feeds base RRP pricebooks per currency (AUD, EUR, GBP, USD) and fixed pricelists per Global-e market to SFCC via MuleSoft. A nightly job generates Global-e-derived pricebooks using FX rates and coefficients from Global-e. Global-e handles shipping charges, duties, and taxes at checkout. SFCC sends the complete cart in the target currency to Global-e. SFCC does **not** independently calculate shipping, duties, or tax for Global-e paths. (REG-040 was retired 05-05 — superseded by REG-041.)

*For checkout-specific frontend behaviour (redirect trigger, data flow), see [checkout.md](checkout.md).*

---

## 4. Currency & Tax (REG-036 – REG-042)

- Single currency per domestic storefront: AUD, USD, GBP, EUR (REG-039). No multi-currency toggle. (Open: Zimmermann would like multi-currency on AU domestic to offer NZD — not yet agreed.)
- Tax display: AU (GST), UK (VAT) via SFCC native tax tables, EU domestic (VAT) via Avalara (REG-037). The EU domestic site supports one RRP but must support multiple EU zone VAT requirements in the order payload. US domestic: prices excl. tax; Avalara calculates sales tax at checkout (REG-038). NZ and New Caledonia on AU: Avalara (REG-037).
- Sale pricing: was/now format. If price changes again after sale, only "now" updates; "was" is retained (REG-042).
- Prices shown in storefront currency on PDP, PLP, mini-cart, cart (REG-036).

---

## 5. EU Locale Billing Fields (REG-011)

The system will display locale-specific additional billing fields where required (e.g. Italian Codice Fiscale or VAT ID). **Open (REG-011):** confirm with Egaltine which other locales (e.g. Spanish NIF, French SIRET) require additional fields. Do not implement until confirmed.

---

## 6. Language & Translation (REG-044 – REG-047)

- EU domestic supports 4 languages: EN, FR, IT, ES (REG-044). All other storefronts English only.
- All customer-facing content (CMS from Contentful, product data from Product API) translated across EU locale variants (REG-045). CMS must accommodate translation-driven adjustments (e.g. button resize for translated CTAs).
- English is the site-wide fallback where translated content is unavailable (REG-046).
- Translation pipeline (REG-047, de-scoped 2026-05-25): the end-to-end configurable pipeline requirement was withdrawn. Translation occurs directly between **Contentful and Transperfect** outside the PWA Kit's concern; any SFCC-held strings (e.g. system messages, validation copy) are translated via static JSON files. No FE work required beyond consuming the translated Contentful payloads.

---

## 7. Consent (Didomi) (REG-048 – REG-056)

- Cookie consent banner shown on first visit on all storefronts, managed by Didomi CMP (REG-048). Consent preferences persist across sessions (REG-050).
- **Do not load any third-party tracking or marketing script until Didomi consent is granted** (REG-049).
- Consent categories: Performance, Analytics, Marketing — Required is non-configurable (REG-051). Subject to legal confirmation but expected to follow existing Didomi process.
- Customers can review and update preferences at any time via the storefront (REG-052). Granular consent allowed — individual categories can be toggled independently (REG-053).

### Per-storefront defaults (REG-054)

| Storefront | Default |
|---|---|
| EU storefronts | Opted-out (no action = opted-out) |
| US domestic | Explicit choice required (no action = opted-out) |
| AU, US international, HK, ME | Opted-in by default |

- GTM integrated with Didomi for **Google Consent Mode v2** signal passing across all storefronts (REG-055).
- Hashed email passed to GTM at order confirmation for Enhanced Conversions (REG-056).
- Didomi consent notice greys out all site content and prevents interaction until the consent flow completes (HPC-013/014).

---

## 8. Marketing Opt-In (REG-057 – REG-059)

- Marketing opt-in checkbox displayed at two points: guest checkout entry page and account registration page. Unchecked by default on all storefronts **except US (pre-checked)** (REG-057).
- Opt-in state sync: FE → SFCC → Omneo → Emarsys. Passed to Omneo on order placement for guests, on account registration for registered customers (REG-058).
- Registered customers can update marketing preferences in My Account → synced to Omneo (REG-059).

*Open: guest checkout journey & marketing opt-in touchpoints (REG-057, REG-058) — see AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies".*

---

## 9. Inside Chat (HPC-039 – HPC-040)

- Customer support chat widget shown on relevant pages per Inside Chat's own display rules.
- Must only be initialised **after Didomi consent** for the relevant category.

---

## 10. GDPR & Privacy (REG-060 – REG-067)

- Right-to-erasure: deletion of customer PII from SFCC including registered accounts, saved addresses, and guest order data (REG-060).
- DSAR and erasure requests managed via the SFCC GDPR cartridge, replacing the current manual legal/IT ticketing process (REG-061).
- Configurable data retention per market in SFCC BM; auto-purge on expiry (REG-062).
- Adyen payment tokens held in SFCC are deleted as part of right-to-erasure (REG-063).

- Consent audit log capturing when and how consent was captured (REG-066).

## 11. Data Migration, SEO, GEO & URL

This content now lives in its own PRD: [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md), covering Magento→SFCC data migration (DMU-001 – DMU-012), URL strategy and redirects (DMU-013 – DMU-020), SEO (DMU-021 – DMU-041), and GEO routing foundations (DMU-042). Storefront routing, consent, and currency remain in this file.

---

## 12. Open Items

See **AGENTS.md "Unresolved Dependencies"** for the full list. Regional open items (data migration / URL / SEO / GEO open items live in [dataMigrationSeo.md](dataMigrationSeo.md)):

**Resolved since previous version:**

1	# PWA Integration Design Documents
2	
3	> **Status:** draft. The confirmed sources of truth are the PRDs and the TSD; this folder is the per-system Detailed Design that builds on them.
4	
5	*Last updated 2026-06-04.*
6	
7	These documents describe each external system that the Zimmermann PWA storefront interacts with **from the PWA layer** — either browser-direct or proxied through the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer. Each system has its own document covering purpose, scope, browser-side architecture, authentication, data exchange, consent gating, performance, multi-region behaviour, graceful degradation, security and privacy, observability, and the open items requiring client input before implementation.
8	
9	> **Scope.** PWA-layer only (browser-direct and MRT-proxied). Backend integrations consumed by SFCC via MuleSoft (NewStore writes, AP21 — including the inbound product + pricing feed, Omneo profile sync, Emarsys, Narvar back office, Avalara, GiveX validate / redeem / refund, Transperfect) are addressed by the SFCC ↔ MuleSoft middleware design and are not duplicated here. **Booxi** (boutique appointment history) is a PWA-direct MRT path (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a MuleSoft flow, and is documented here in [06-booxi.md](06-booxi.md).
10	
11	The documents are grouped by role rather than by runtime load order. A reader new to the system can start at the top and build a mental model from the most central systems outwards.
12	
13	### Commerce backbone
14	
15	The data sources every storefront page depends on.
16	
17	| # | System | Purpose | Document |
18	|---|---|---|---|
19	| 1 | **Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI)** | All commerce data — catalogue, basket, customer, orders. | [01-sfcc.md](01-sfcc.md) |
20	| 2 | **Contentful** | CMS — Delivery API, Preview API, Studio live preview, publish webhook. | [02-contentful.md](02-contentful.md) |
21	
22	### Account and customer data
23	
24	Server-mediated reads that bypass SFCC for data the storefront fetches on behalf of the customer.
25	
26	| # | System | Purpose | Document |
27	|---|---|---|---|
28	| 3 | **MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads)** | Order history, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock via MRT proxy. | [03-mulesoft.md](03-mulesoft.md) |
29	| 4 | **Omneo** | Communication Preferences iFrame in My Account. | [04-omneo.md](04-omneo.md) |
30	| 5 | **GiveX (balance check)** | My Account gift card balance check via MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX. | [05-givex.md](05-givex.md) |
31	| 6 | **Booxi** | My Account boutique appointment history via MRT proxy (PWA → MRT → Booxi). Scope/timeline TBC. | [06-booxi.md](06-booxi.md) |
32	
33	### Checkout cluster
34	
35	The buying flow.
36	
37	| # | System | Purpose | Document |
38	|---|---|---|---|

# PWA Integration Design Documents

> **Status:** draft. The confirmed sources of truth are the PRDs and the TSD; this folder is the per-system Detailed Design that builds on them.

*Last updated 2026-06-04.*

These documents describe each external system that the Zimmermann PWA storefront interacts with **from the PWA layer** — either browser-direct or proxied through the PWA's Managed Runtime Node layer. Each system has its own document covering purpose, scope, browser-side architecture, authentication, data exchange, consent gating, performance, multi-region behaviour, graceful degradation, security and privacy, observability, and the open items requiring client input before implementation.

> **Scope.** PWA-layer only (browser-direct and MRT-proxied). Backend integrations consumed by SFCC via MuleSoft (NewStore writes, AP21 — including the inbound product + pricing feed, Omneo profile sync, Emarsys, Narvar back office, Avalara, GiveX validate / redeem / refund, Transperfect) are addressed by the SFCC ↔ MuleSoft middleware design and are not duplicated here. **Booxi** (boutique appointment history) is a PWA-direct MRT path (PWA → MRT → Booxi), not a MuleSoft flow, and is documented here in [06-booxi.md](06-booxi.md).

The documents are grouped by role rather than by runtime load order. A reader new to the system can start at the top and build a mental model from the most central systems outwards.

### Commerce backbone

The data sources every storefront page depends on.

| # | System | Purpose | Document |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SCAPI)** | All commerce data — catalogue, basket, customer, orders. | [01-sfcc.md](01-sfcc.md) |
| 2 | **Contentful** | CMS — Delivery API, Preview API, Studio live preview, publish webhook. | [02-contentful.md](02-contentful.md) |

### Account and customer data

Server-mediated reads that bypass SFCC for data the storefront fetches on behalf of the customer.

| # | System | Purpose | Document |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | **MuleSoft (PWA-direct reads)** | Order history, order detail, returns, real-time boutique stock via MRT proxy. | [03-mulesoft.md](03-mulesoft.md) |
| 4 | **Omneo** | Communication Preferences iFrame in My Account. | [04-omneo.md](04-omneo.md) |
| 5 | **GiveX (balance check)** | My Account gift card balance check via MRT → MuleSoft → GiveX. | [05-givex.md](05-givex.md) |
| 6 | **Booxi** | My Account boutique appointment history via MRT proxy (PWA → MRT → Booxi). Scope/timeline TBC. | [06-booxi.md](06-booxi.md) |

### Checkout cluster

The buying flow.

| # | System | Purpose | Document |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | **Adyen** | Browser-side payment Drop-in for SFCC-owned domestic checkout. | [07-adyen.md](07-adyen.md) |
| 8 | **Global-e** | International checkout (HK, ME, EU international, US international). | [08-global-e.md](08-global-e.md) |
| 9 | **Google Maps Platform (Places)** | Address autocomplete at checkout, MRT-proxied. | [09-google-maps.md](09-google-maps.md) |
| 10 | **Google reCAPTCHA** | Bot protection on register / login forms — browser loads script, MRT verifies token server-side. | [10-recaptcha.md](10-recaptcha.md) |
| 11 | **Narvar** | Estimated Delivery Date widget at checkout, domestic only. | [11-narvar.md](11-narvar.md) |

### Cross-cutting overlays

Consent, analytics, and customer service — applied across every page rather than tied to a specific journey.

| # | System | Purpose | Document |
|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | **Didomi** | Consent Management Platform — gatekeeper for every browser-loaded third-party script. | [12-didomi.md](12-didomi.md) |
| 13 | **Google Tag Manager** | Data layer, Consent Mode v2, downstream tag orchestration via Tell No Lies. | [13-gtm.md](13-gtm.md) |
| 14 | **Inside Chat** | Customer-service chat widget. | [14-inside-chat.md](14-inside-chat.md) |
| 15 | **Optimizely Web** | A/B testing and personalisation — frontend-direct script (not in GTM). | [15-optimizely.md](15-optimizely.md) |
| 16 | **Crazy Egg** | Heatmaps and session recording — frontend-direct script (not in GTM). | [16-crazyegg.md](16-crazyegg.md) |
| 17 | **Measmerize** | Find My Size widget + size guide overlay on PDP. | [17-measmerize.md](17-measmerize.md) |
| 18 | **Vimeo** | Product video (PDP gallery) and editorial video (homepage and content pages via Contentful CMS). | [18-vimeo.md](18-vimeo.md) |

## Note on runtime load order

The ordering above is **for reading**, not for runtime. At runtime, **Didomi loads first** (document 11) because every other browser-loaded third-party script — GTM, Inside Chat, the Narvar widget, the Google Maps proxy call, and the Adyen Drop-in — is gated by Didomi consent. Each integration document records its own consent posture; the Didomi document is the single contract that all the others honour.

## Cross-cutting principles

- **Fail closed on consent.** If Didomi cannot determine consent state, no third-party tracking or marketing script loads.
- **Fail independently.** One vendor outage must not break the storefront — each integration has a documented degradation path.
- **LCP budget is ≤ 2.0 s at p75 mobile.** Any browser-loaded third-party script defers behind consent or hydration and does not block first paint.
- **Multi-region.** Seven SFCC sites across six regions, eleven active locales. Every integration that varies by region documents the per-storefront configuration matrix.
- **No secrets in the browser bundle.** Public and publishable keys only — anything that grants write access lives server-side, either in MRT environment variables or in SFCC Business Manager.

## Document template

Each integration document follows the same structure for ease of review:

1. Purpose and scope
2. Vendor relationship
3. Browser-side architecture
4. Authentication and credentials
5. Data exchanged
6. Consent and gating
7. Performance and loading strategy
8. Multi-region behaviour
9. Failure modes and graceful degradation
10. Security and privacy
11. Observability
12. Open items requiring client confirmation

Sections may merge where the surface is narrow (for example, the GiveX document folds observability into the security and privacy section).

# Integration Open Items — Consolidated

Open items requiring client confirmation across the fifteen external integrations in scope for the Zimmermann PWA storefront. Each item is a decision, contract, credential, or sign-off that must land before the corresponding integration can be implemented end-to-end against a real account.

## Summary

We need their documentations or implementation guide for at least:
Omneo iframe (for communication preferences), Booxi, MuleSoft (for GiveX balance check, order history/detail, returns).

Then for all the external systems (also incl. Adyen, Global-e, Google Maps, reCAPTCHA, Narvar, Didomi, GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Measmerize) we'll need their relevant Zimmermann-specific IDs, for each environment (dev/uat/prod etc) if applicable, and their associated Didomi feature/vendor ID if consent-gated.

Plus:
- GiveX: Do we need reCAPTCHA for balance check?
- CAI-023 Can MuleSoft aggregate stock?

| # | Integration | Items |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | SFCC | 2 |
| 2 | Contentful | 3 |
| 3 | MuleSoft | 4 |
| 4 | Omneo | 3 (all hard blockers) |
| 5 | GiveX | 3 |
| 6 | Booxi | 4 (scope/timeline TBC) |
| 7 | Adyen | 2 |
| 8 | Global-e | 2 |
| 9 | Google Maps | 1 |
| 10 | reCAPTCHA | 2 |
| 11 | Narvar | 2 |
| 12 | Didomi | 2 |
| 13 | GTM | 2 |
| 14 | Inside Chat | 0 |
| 15 | Optimizely | 1 |
| 16 | Crazy Egg | 3 |
| 17 | Measmerize | 2 |
| 18 | Vimeo | 2 |

Total: 40 items across 18 integrations.

---

## 1. SFCC

1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.

2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) assumes `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to a different origin than the SCAPI host (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). If they share an origin the two pools should be merged.

## 2. Contentful

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all seven storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). Not yet confirmed is the split on pages that compose both: which editorial blocks appear on the PDP and PLP and whether any are authored in SFCC Page Designer rather than Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu carries Contentful-authored promotional tiles alongside the SFCC category tree. Zimmermann and merchandising to confirm the per-surface split so the PDP, PLP, and navigation components can be built against a fixed data-source contract. The working assumption is captured in the content-ownership boundary table in the Contentful integration design (§1).
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provision the Space and supply per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be exercised against a real Contentful environment.

## 3. MuleSoft

1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).
4. **CAI-023 — warehouse + boutique stock aggregation for browse-level availability.** Confirm whether MuleSoft can deliver a pre-aggregated available-to-promise figure combining warehouse and eligible boutique stock, to drive the Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock states on PDP and PLP. If MuleSoft cannot pre-aggregate, the storefront must decide whether to request both sources separately and aggregate client-side (extra round-trip) or fall back to SFCC-only inventory. This is distinct from the cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) and the Find in Boutique flyout (CAI-038), both of which have their own endpoints. **Owner:** Integration team (Tryzens / MuleSoft).

## 4. Omneo

No Omneo-issued identifiers, hosts, or credentials are currently in Accenture's possession. All three items below are needed before implementation can begin against a real Omneo tenant; all three are hard blockers.

1. **Communication Preferences iFrame — confirm the non-Shopify auth handshake.** CRM-174 confirms the screen is rendered as an Omneo iFrame; the iFrame contains Communication Preferences, region/country selection (location, state, and language preference), and three clickable images that open the respective PLP within the iFrame (PLP-in-iFrame behaviour is an enhancement, not in scope for launch). Omneo documents embedding the Profile Portal as an iframe dialog — so the embed itself is a supported Omneo capability. However, Omneo's documented embed is a Shopify theme extension that authenticates via the Omneo CX Shopify app proxy, which a PWA does not have. Confirm, for the non-Shopify embed on Zimmermann's plan: the Profile Portal embed URL, how the Communication Preferences and region/country selection views are scoped within it, and the auth handshake outside Shopify (a customer-scoped signed-URL / HMAC approach, or a server-minted customer-scoped token). If no embed path is available, the fallback is a redirect to the hosted portal or a native rebuild against Omneo's API.
2. **Omneo identifiers and embed URL.** Provide the values needed to construct the iFrame `src` for production and each non-production environment:
   - Omneo tenant / account identifier (the value that appears in the embed URL, e.g. the account subdomain or path slug)
   - Exact embed URL host(s) and path(s) for the Communication Preferences widget — needed both to build the iFrame and to add to the storefront's `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` and `connect-src` allowlist
   - Any other public identifier the widget requires (widget ID, environment ID, configuration key)
3. **HMAC signing secret (or token mechanism).** Provide the per-environment secret/credential Omneo issues for the customer-scoped embed auth. Without it the Omneo ID proxy authentication cannot be exercised end-to-end; until it is provided, the integration can only be developed against a mock.

## 5. GiveX

1. **MuleSoft balance-check HTTPS contract.** The integration team to publish the request and response schema for the MuleSoft balance-check endpoint (`POST /givex/balance` placeholder) — the request carries both the card number and the PIN (secure PINs are enabled) — plus the error taxonomy that maps GiveX failure codes to the GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061 customer-facing messages, including the invalid-PIN case. Without this contract the storefront cannot implement the call against a real MuleSoft instance. **Owner:** MuleSoft — GiveX supplies the underlying failure-code list; Zimmermann owns the final customer-facing message copy.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route. **Owner:** MuleSoft (host / token / thresholds); the MRT-edge WAF / bot / rate-limit config is ours.
3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT balance-check route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request — this is not yet decided. If a CAPTCHA is used, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login (no new provisioning). **Owner:** Zimmermann.

## 6. Booxi

Boutique appointment history is a PWA-direct read (PWA → MRT → Booxi); scope and timeline are TBC.

1. **Storefront scope and timeline (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope, and confirm the target sprint. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments — whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC / Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

## 7. Adyen

1. **Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs.** Provide the Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs per domain. Needed before the wallet buttons can be switched on. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
2. **Per-environment Adyen credentials.** Provide, for each environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod): client key, API key, HMAC key, merchant account ID per region, and whether it's a test or live Adyen account. Without these, checkout can't be tested against a real Adyen account.
## 8. Global-e

1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply: (a) the `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers; and (b) the `postMessage` schema and trusted sender origin for iframe resize and order-completion signals — the PWA listener must verify `event.origin` against this value before acting. Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.

2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order, to decide between rendering full order detail or a "View on tracking page" fallback. Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.

## 9. Google Maps

1. **Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project and per-environment API keys.** Zimmermann to provision one Places API key per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without the keys the integration cannot be exercised against a real Google account.

## 10. reCAPTCHA

1. **Per-environment reCAPTCHA site key and secret key.** Zimmermann to provision a Google Cloud project (or use an existing one) and register reCAPTCHA v3 keys for each environment's domain. Supply `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (public) and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (server-only, for MRT token verification) per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without these, bot protection cannot be exercised against a real Google account.

2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID (EU and UK storefronts only).** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated in EU and UK. Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers reCAPTCHA (no obvious prior — the purpose is bot protection, not analytics or marketing). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated script loader can be wired correctly. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.

## 11. Narvar

1. **Per-environment Narvar retailer ID and CONVERT API key.** Provide one set per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod). Without these the widget cannot be exercised against a real Narvar account.

2. **Didomi consent category for Narvar Promise.** Confirm which Didomi category the CONVERT widget falls under (Performance?). This determines whether the widget loads for EU and UK users who accept Performance cookies but decline Analytics or Marketing.

## 12. Didomi

1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT / Prod) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.

## 13. GTM (with Tell No Lies/Zimm)

1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). Zimmermann/Accenture to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** The data layer is a single shared artifact. Tell No Lies to confirm the storefront's proposed event and attribute schema (page views, product impressions, add-to-cart, begin-checkout, purchase and related ecommerce events, plus consent state and user identifiers) satisfies both GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) and the frontend-direct data-layer consumers (Optimizely, Crazy Egg — not GTM tags). Any additional attributes Optimizely needs for segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg needs for filtering (AAB-005) must be raised at this point.

## 14. Inside Chat

No open items — PWA has zero Inside-Chat work.

## 15. Optimizely (with Zimm/TNL)

Optimizely Web is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent.

1. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Optimizely (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

## 16. Crazy Egg (with Zimm/TNL)

Crazy Egg (heatmaps / session recording) is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent (category TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm).

1. **Crazy Egg account / site ID per environment.** Zimmermann to provide the account / site ID (script), confirming whether a single account serves all environments or one per tier.
2. **Masking configuration ownership.** Confirm that Tell No Lies owns and applies the session-recording masking configuration (payment and PII fields suppressed) inside the Crazy Egg application. The storefront-side scope is confirmed (AAB-005): the PWA populates the data layer and renders maskable fields with stable selectors; masking itself is outside the PWA.
3. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Crazy Egg (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.

## 17. Measmerize

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm which of two approaches applies: (a) load the script freely and call `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` / `disableCustom()` / `cookies.disableFunctional()` when consent is denied (Essential cookies always run), or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Zimmermann Privacy to also confirm the Didomi consent category and Tell No Lies to supply the corresponding Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
2. **Brand code UUIDs.** Script URL (`https://client.measmerize.com/script.js`) and product identifier (SFCC SKU, `data-product-code`) are confirmed from vendor docs. Measmerize issues exactly two brand codes per retailer: one for production and one shared across all non-production environments (Dev / SIT / Stage / UAT). Measmerize to supply both values to be set as MRT environment variables. **Owner:** Zimmermann / Measmerize.

## 18. Vimeo

Vimeo is used for product video (PDP) and editorial video (content pages via Contentful CMS). The embed loads client-side as a facade-loaded iframe.

1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm: (a) always append `dnt=1` to the embed URL — suppresses Vimeo's tracking cookies, no Didomi gate needed; or (b) load the standard embed gated behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

2. **Vimeo platform confirmation (PRD-067).** The Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the video platform, but PRD-067 is explicitly open: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed — open action to confirm best solution for smoothest FE experience." content.text:
Both the playbook and a direct look at the codebase turned up more than expected — including some corrections that go beyond what the playbook itself already caught. Here's the revision, plus what needs to change in the companion context doc for the instructions to actually be grounded.

## Name

**Keep "Zimmermann Second Brain."** The name is already scope-agnostic — it's the description doing the scoping, not the name — so widening scope to the delivery/code layer doesn't strain it. Renaming would just cost continuity with existing conversation history for no real gain.

## Description

```
Engagement-wide knowledge base and thinking partner for the Zimmermann × Accenture Song SFCC replatform (plus the Website Redesign and Contentful workstreams) — and for the delivery effort building it. Spans the solution and Discovery decks, both SOWs, the estimator/scope workbooks, the TSDs, the UX review, the kickoff pack, the open-items tracker, and the Frontend Lead Playbook (delivery methodology plus facts verified against the live zimmermann-pwa repo) — for Q&A, ideation, solutioning, and FE-Lead delivery coaching, with strict provenance and document-status discipline spanning both the contracted-scope and as-built layers.
```

## Instructions

```
## What this project is

A working knowledge base and thinking partner for the entire Zimmermann × Accenture Song engagement — the Salesforce Commerce Cloud (SFCC) replatform of Zimmermann's storefront off Magento 2, plus the two workstreams running alongside it (the Work & Co Website Redesign and the Contentful headless-CMS build) — and the delivery effort building it, now that the Frontend Lead Playbook is in scope. Use it to answer questions, connect the material, ideate, evaluate options, draft solutions, and think through FE-Lead delivery/leadership questions — not only to look things up. It is no longer scoped to the V2.0 solution deck; that deck is one document among many, and the repo itself is no longer scoped to commercial/planning documents alone.

Two distinct kinds of material live here now, and they answer different kinds of questions:
- **Planned / contracted layer** — the decks, both SOWs, the estimator, the TSDs, the UX review, the kickoff pack, openItems.md. These describe what was scoped, sold, designed, or is blocked — as of their own dates.
- **Delivery / as-built layer** — the Frontend Lead Playbook. Its sections 1–15 are delivery methodology (dual IC/Lead craft, largely stack-agnostic); its section 16 is a bridge that has been verified line-by-line against the actual zimmermann-pwa codebase (2026-07-09) — squad code-ownership, integration counts, CI/CD gates, auth implementation, and other as-built facts the planning docs could only describe prospectively.

The live codebase itself is not uploaded here — Claude.ai can't inspect a running repo — but the Playbook's section 16 is the verified bridge to it. If a question needs codebase-level ground truth beyond what section 16 captured, say so plainly rather than guessing; that's a job for Claude Code against the actual repo, not this project.

## Ground everything in the repository first

Answer from the uploaded material before anything else, and say which document(s) it came from. The repo spans decks, SOWs, TSDs, estimator/scope workbooks, a UX review, a kickoff pack, a live open-items tracker, and the Frontend Lead Playbook — see the project context doc for the full list, dates, and status. If something genuinely isn't in the repo (a general SFCC / MRT / PWA Kit / Contentful concept, an industry benchmark, a vendor's public docs), answer it, but say plainly it's outside the source rather than blending it into the repo's claims. A third case now exists too: a question about the as-built zimmermann-pwa codebase that goes beyond what the Playbook's section 16 verified — don't extrapolate from decks or guess at code you can't see; say it needs a live-repo check via Claude Code. Keep every one of these seams visible — especially when ideating, always distinguish what the docs say, what the Playbook verified against code, and what you're proposing.

## Provenance and status discipline — the load-bearing rule

The repo's whole value depends on this. Most documents carry a "Conversion notes (read this first)" section and inline "Audit correction" / flag callouts; these are authoritative and must be honored, not smoothed over. Generalize that discipline to everything:

Track verification level per claim: verified (corroborated across sources or from an authoritative artifact), asserted (stated once, uncorroborated), inferred (a reasonable read, not stated), flagged-open (explicitly uncertain). Never state a flagged-uncertain, inferred, or contradicted item as settled fact.
Track document status: current/adopted, draft, superseded/earlier-stage. The repo deliberately holds superseded material (e.g. the May-26 Discovery deliverables and their "WC 25 May" timeline) next to what was adopted. Don't quote a dead date, price, or roster as if it's live.
When documents disagree, surface it — don't silently pick one. Say which doc says what, with its date/status, note which is more likely authoritative and why, and leave genuinely-unreconciled items (e.g. the three contract values) side by side rather than falsely resolved.

This discipline applies to the Playbook exactly as it does to any deck — including to its own most-verified section. Section 16 states outright that it can go stale ("it went stale once already without anyone noticing") and asks to be re-checked quarterly or after any major architecture change, new integration wave, or squad-ownership shake-up. Treat its facts as verified as of 2026-07-09, not verified permanently — check its own re-verification date before leaning on it for anything time-sensitive, the same way you'd check a deck's revision date.

## Recency / authority defaults (confirm rather than assume as the repo grows)

- Timeline, roster, sprint model, epics → Kickoff Pack (6 Jul 2026) and the SOW register supersede the Discovery Final Deliverables (May-26). Adopted start ~6 Jul 2026.
- Contract value → genuinely contested; present all three, none cleanly authoritative.
- Technical design / integration behavior → the two TSDs (Jun-26 drafts) over the decks' high-level diagrams — but see the new bullet below when the question is about the actual code, not the design intent.
- Live blockers / integration open items → openItems.md. Its numbers and even its self-contradictions match the codebase's own .docs/temp/openItems.md closely enough that this is very likely the same tracker, not an independent business-side summary — treat it as the live engineering blocker list, not just a status report about one.
- **As-built engineering facts (stack specifics, squad code-ownership, integration counts, CI/CD gates, auth implementation) → the Frontend Lead Playbook section 16, verified against the live repo (2026-07-09), outranks the decks'/SOW's higher-level or earlier-stage claims where they overlap.** The decks describe what was designed or planned; section 16 describes what's actually there. Where it corrects a deck claim outright (e.g. the old "14 integrations, four MuleSoft connector patterns" figure), treat the deck claim as superseded, not as an alternate valid lens — but always check section 16's own re-verification date first (see Provenance discipline above).

## How to work here

- Connect across documents. RACI ↔ team roster ↔ SOW responsibilities; environment strategy ↔ CI/CD; open items / risk ↔ pricing and contingency; estimator units ↔ scope counts ↔ contract value; UX decisions ↔ epics ↔ Gantt; and now also: squad roster (Kickoff Pack) ↔ squad code ownership (Playbook §16 / CODEOWNERS) — two different questions that use the same "Squad A/B" language and shouldn't be conflated; and the Estimator's explicit exclusions (accessibility, broader perf, e2e/cross-browser) ↔ what the repo's own tooling already has in place for exactly those categories — worth flagging when the two don't line up. The value is in the joins.
- Explain the why behind a decision when it's inferable — and say when it isn't and is simply asserted.
- Review, don't recite. Surface gaps, unstated assumptions, and internal inconsistencies the way you'd review someone else's design doc. Flag a real gap or risk the moment you spot it, mid-answer.
- Ideation and solutioning are in scope now. Sketch approaches, weigh options, draft artifacts (designs, plans, stories, code) — grounded in the repo, with the grounded/proposed seam kept visible. This now includes FE-Lead delivery-methodology work: drafting a story template, a review-culture ritual, a rules-layer fix, or a CODEOWNERS/registry correction — grounded in what the Playbook and its section 16 actually say, with the same seam discipline.

## Modes

Default to a working thinking-partner, not a tutor. Keep learning affordances available on request: if asked, quiz or walk through a section Socratically rather than only lecturing, and layer explanations concept-first, detail-second. This applies as much to the Playbook's delivery-methodology content (the four anti-agreeableness techniques, the build loop, the section 16.4 live gap-hunts) as to the commercial/technical material.

## Stack note (project-specific)

The Zimmermann storefront is React 18 on Salesforce PWA Kit / Managed Runtime, extending @salesforce/retail-react-app v10.0.0 via a slim overrides/ layer (TypeScript-only inside it — no fork), Chakra UI first with design tokens in overrides/app/theme/foundation/, TypeScript strict — not Angular. Match that stack when writing or reviewing code. The engineering standards from the global preferences still apply (strict TS / no any, reactive patterns, clean separation, maintainability over cleverness, call out framework gotchas) — just for React/PWA Kit, flagging PWA-Kit-specific concerns (overrides-vs-config, SSR/CSR split, MRT proxy boundary, upgrade-impact of overrides).

Verified specifics worth knowing before reviewing or proposing code (Playbook §16, confirmed against the live repo):

- SSR layer is split out of ssr.js into overrides/app/ssr/: slasTokens.ts (SLAS auth — wrong change breaks auth site-wide), contentSecurityPolicy.ts (CSP headers — wrong change opens a security hole on every page), connectionPools.ts (undici pool isolation), paymentMetadata.ts, marketingCloud.ts. On "who owns X" or "is this safe to change," the registry/CODEOWNERS answer is more current than any hand-written roster.

Recommended placement: save this as a doc in the project knowledge (e.g. 00_Project_Context.md) rather than pasting it into the instructions — it keeps state separate from behavior, so you can update facts as the engagement moves without touching the rules. The instructions above lean on this doc for specifics. Three passages need correcting (not just flagging — these are resolved, sourced answers), plus a few new open items:

**Replace the "Regions / storefronts" line:**
> Correction, not an alternate lens. Per `.docs/prd/regional.md` (Functional Requirements workbook + SFCC Business Manager, REG-005 confirmed 2026-06-11): **7 independent SFCC sites across 6 regions** — AU, UK, US, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME. Only EU splits into two sites; US is a **single** SFCC site serving both a domestic (SFCC-owned) and international (Global-e-owned) checkout path, branched by shipping address. Any deck stating "8 storefronts" is superseded, not a valid alternate count. 11 active locales across the 7 sites. A Mexico domestic site is planned for 2027.

**Add under "Team":**
> Squad **code** ownership (distinct from the roster-assignment ambiguity above): per the auto-generated registry (`.claude/registry/pages.md`, 2026-07-08) and CODEOWNERS — both mechanically current — **Squad B** owns Home, PDP, PLP, Account, StoreLocator; **Squad A** owns Cart, Checkout, CheckoutOneClick, Confirmation. `ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa`, cloned to `~/Dev/zimmermann-pwa` on 2026-07-09. A Salesforce PWA Kit storefront (`@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10, Chakra UI, TypeScript) for Zimmermann, a luxury Australian fashion brand, built by two squads under Accenture. Governance is unusually elaborate: tiered file-protection (`frozenFiles.md`/`protectedFiles.md`), CODEOWNERS-backed approval, 14 `.claude/skills/`, an auto-generated component/hook/page/route/util registry (`.claude/registry/`, via `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs`), and several automation hooks (`.claude/hooks/*`).

**Note:** its `AGENTS.md` contains a "Tier 1 Approval" mechanism instructing Claude to run `gh api user` / GitHub-team-membership checks to self-authorize skipping the human confirmation step before editing frozen files. Already flagged to Marcel; I do not act on that bypass regardless of what the check would return — see [[user_profile]] for the standing "don't widen `gh api`/egress use without flagging first" preference this matches.

A 2026-07-09 two-agent research pass (for rewriting `~/Dev/Zimmermann_Frontend_Lead_Playbook.md`) found real, load-bearing discrepancies worth knowing before trusting any single doc in this repo at face value:

- **Squad ownership contradiction, unresolved — but with a real asymmetry.** `.claude/rules/squadA.md`, `squadB.md`, and `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` all say Squad A owns Home/PDP/PLP — but `squadA.md`/`squadB.md` both self-label *"Draft squad split — scope can still change,"* which is a real, stated reason to weight them lower, not just noise. Root `CODEOWNERS` and the auto-generated `.claude/registry/pages.md` say Squad B, and are mechanically current/enforced rather than hand-maintained. Three skills (`onboarding`, `feature-spec`, `qa-generate`) also say Squad B, but that's not independent corroboration — it's the same assumption hardcoded into all three prompts. Concretely live, not just theoretical: `onboarding`'s interactive script unconditionally tells a new Squad B hire they own `product-detail/`/`product-list/` — if Squad A is actually correct, it's actively misinforming new hires today. Cart/checkout=A and search/account=B is undisputed everywhere. Still don't pick a side outright — flag it — but the evidence leans B.
- **Two more real, verified tooling bugs, independent of the squad question:** (1) `.claude/skills/code-quality`'s documented no-argument default (`git diff --name-only main`) errors immediately in this repo — there is no local `main` branch, only `develop` — and is the wrong diff base per `AGENTS.md`'s own branch model even when it resolves; `pr-checklist` (which calls code-quality internally) correctly diffs against `develop` instead. (2) `contentful-register-component`/`contentful-drift-check` (and likely `weekly-agents.yml`'s contentful-drift-audit job) assume components register via a co-located `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` file, but the 3 components actually live in Contentful Studio today (`CollectionHero`, `ImageText`, `ShoppableImage`) are inlined in one array in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` instead — no `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` file exists anywhere in the repo. Running drift-check today silently checks zero pairs; a clean report means "nothing matched the pattern," not "no drift."
- **Smaller confirmed-but-not-fixed oddities, for awareness:** `.claude/skills/session-start`'s own memory table mis-locates `architecture.md` (says `.docs/memory/`, it's actually `.docs/architecture.md`) and references a `.docs/memory/userProfile.md` that doesn't exist anywhere in the repo (also referenced by `.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh`'s candidate list) — a phantom file two mechanisms both assume is real. `project-init`/parts of the E2E scaffold still assume a `ZIM`/`ZIM-000` Jira prefix; the repo already settled on `SFCC` (e.g. `SFCC-000_guest-checkout`). `e2e/` specs are `.js`, not `.ts`, contradicting `qa-generate`'s and `testing.md`'s own stated TS-only rule for E2E.
- **Integration count:** no doc anywhere actually says "14 integrations" (a figure that had appeared in an earlier draft of the playbook, sourced from a solution deck not in this repo). Real counts: 18 PWA-layer integrations per `.docs/temp/integration/index.md` and `.docs/memory/projectState.md`; ~28 if counting server-to-server/out-of-band systems per `.docs/architecture.md`. `.docs/temp/openItems.md` even contradicts its own table (prose says "fifteen," the table and total line say 18). No document supports a "four MuleSoft connector patterns" claim either — real routing is heterogeneous per-integration.
- **Aspirational vs. real:** `.docs/planning/sharedAiBrainBrief.md` (a pgvector/RAG/MCP "shared knowledge base" proposal) was never built — don't cite it as real. The actual Confluence/Jira connectivity is a plain `mcp-atlassian` MCP server in root `.mcp.json`. Similarly `.docs/memory/feedback.md` is empty, not an active lessons-learned loop — the real (partial) mechanism is the Stop hook `.claude/hooks/session-reflect.sh`, which drafts dated proposals into `.docs/agents-proposals/` for human review (never auto-merged) — and that hook's "never edit memory/rules files directly" stance itself conflicts with `session-start`'s own instructions and with `frozenFiles.md` (which doesn't list `.docs/memory/*` as Tier 1). Unreconciled, not just undocumented.

**Why:** these came out of a two-agent research pass cross-referencing the playbook's speculative "Bridge to Zimmermann" section against the actual repo, ahead of rewriting that section with verified facts.

**How to apply:** Don't take `squadA.md`/`squadB.md`, the "14 integrations" figure, or `sharedAiBrainBrief.md` at face value in future work here — cross-check against CODEOWNERS / `.claude/registry/` / `.mcp.json` as the more current, mechanically-enforced sources. See [[project-manndotfiles]] for the separate personal-vs-project Claude Code config distinction (manndotfiles = Marcel's global tool config; this repo's `.claude/` + `AGENTS.md` = the team's shared project contract).

`Zimmermann Second Brain` is a Claude.ai Project (not this repo — a separate claude.ai knowledge-base project) holding the Zimmermann × Accenture Song engagement's business/planning corpus: the solution and Discovery decks, both SOWs, the estimator/scope workbooks, the two TSDs, the UX review, the kickoff pack, and a live open-items tracker — 12 knowledge docs + binaries + ~50 reference images. Its instructions enforce strict provenance (verified/asserted/inferred/flagged-open) and document-status (current/draft/superseded) discipline, and a "recency/authority defaults" table saying which doc wins when sources disagree.

**2026-07-09 revision:** the project already had the Frontend Lead Playbook (`~/Dev/Zimmermann_Frontend_Lead_Playbook.md`) uploaded as file #12, but the instructions didn't yet say how to use it or weigh it against the business docs. Revised the project's description and instructions to add a second authority axis: for *as-built engineering facts* (stack specifics, squad code-ownership, integration counts, CI/CD gates), the Playbook's §16 (verified against the live [[project-zimmermann-pwa]] repo) now outranks the decks/SOW, which only describe what was planned/contracted — while contractual facts (price, contracted scope, milestones) remain deck/SOW-owned regardless. Also corrected several specific facts the business docs got wrong per the live repo (storefront count 7-not-8, squad page-ownership, integration-count scope-ambiguity) — see [[project-zimmermann-pwa]]'s 2026-07-09 continuation entry for the sourcing on each.

**Why:** the business-planning corpus and the delivery/code-verified corpus need different trust rules — a deck's "8 storefronts" and the live PRD's "7, confirmed" aren't two valid lenses on the same fact, one is simply superseded. Folding the Playbook in without a stated authority rule would have left the project silently blending planned-scope claims with as-built ones.

**How to apply:** When asked to work on or query the Second Brain project again, expect it now spans both layers — check which kind of question is being asked (planned/contracted vs. as-built) before deciding which source wins. The project's companion `00_Project_Context.md` doc (recommended-but-not-confirmed to exist as a saved file) is where the detailed facts live; the instructions only hold the abstract authority rules. If asked to revise this project again, re-check the Playbook's own §16 re-verification date first — it can go stale, and the whole point of the revision was to stop treating any single doc as permanently authoritative.
